observations: A dark rounded head-form sits left of center against a flat coral-red field; an orange vertical block occupies the left edge with a darker shadow shape behind the head.
Yellow zigzag lines run horizontally across the mid-face and along the bottom edge; blue segmented dashes arc above the head and cluster at the chin and base in chain-like marks.
The mouth area shows tightly packed white vertical strokes rimmed above and below by looping yellow lines; orange and yellow oval spikes radiate from the upper-right of the head.
reading: The dark mass holds its ground against a hot coral field, its surface layered with crossing marks in red, yellow, and blue that read as both decoration and agitation. A horizontal yellow zigzag pierces the face, while spiked ovals along the crown push outward. The white tooth-row, bounded by looping yellow lines above and below, gives the mouth a fixed, bared quality that reads as a shout or a grin.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #210 and nnxyz nnotb #212 show how differently the same head-form can be handled: #210 packs a cool dark ground with dense multicolor lines; #212 strips back to a silhouette on open blue.

connections.reason: Both works build a dark rounded head-form covered in layered crossing lines, but #210 uses a cool dark ground with white outlines dominating, while #211 sets comparable density against a warm coral field with yellow zigzags as the loudest mark.

nifty faces #96 shares a warm orange ground and a tooth-row rimmed in yellow, offering a cross-collection contrast of how similar mouth marks and background color read at lower line density and with geometric rather than rounded head structure.

lookingQuestion: Where does your eye settle first — on the horizontal yellow zigzag cutting across the face, the spiked ovals along the crown, or the white tooth-row at the mouth — and what does that path through the marks suggest about how the image is organized?
ambiguities: The orange vertical block at the left edge may be a separate background element or a shadow cast by the head-form; the image alone does not resolve this.

Title order and recorded creation order align for this work and its immediate neighbors in the owned subset, but gaps elsewhere in the nnotb family mean this alignment cannot be assumed collection-wide.
